children: President Donald Trump’s economic approval rating has fallen to a record low, while government corruption has emerged as Americans’ top concern ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, according to CNBC’s latest All-America Economic Survey.
Trump’s overall approval rating remained relatively stable at 40%, with 59% disapproving. However, his net approval rating of minus 19 percentage points compares with minus 8 points a year ago.

His economic approval has deteriorated more sharply, dropping to 34% from 38% in July, while disapproval climbed to 65% from 60%. The resulting net economic approval of minus 31 points marks his weakest rating across either term, according to the survey.

Meanwhile, government corruption topped the list of voters’ concerns, cited by 36% of respondents, narrowly ahead of food and grocery costs at 34%. Protecting democracy and gasoline prices each ranked at 23%.

The survey also found broad opposition to potential conflicts of interest involving public officials. Some 93% of respondents said elected officials, including the president and members of Congress, should not be allowed to personally own or trade individual stocks in companies holding federal contracts. Another 89% opposed federal contracts going to companies owned or backed by a sitting president’s immediate family.
The poll of 1,000 registered voters was conducted October 14-18 and co-led by Democratic pollster Hart Research Associates and Republican pollster Public Opinion Strategies.
It found Americans preferring Democratic control of Congress by a 52% to 45% margin. The 7 percentage point Democratic edge represents a 3 percentage point gain for Democrats from the July survey.

title: Trump’s economic approval hits all-time low, corruption tops voter concerns ahead of midterms - CNBC
